tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: propose it and call this.

The result says which case below applies. When the box shows your question, it ends your turn: write no text after this call, since the recap and question say what the user needs and your work above holds the detail. Otherwise your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, with any question the box did not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

## tradingview
TradingView MCP — 78 tools for reading and controlling a live TradingView Desktop chart.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE — use this to pick the right tool:

Reading your chart:
- chart_get_state → get symbol, timeframe, all indicator names + entity IDs (call first)
- data_get_study_values → get current numeric values from ALL visible indicators (RSI, MACD, BB, EMA, etc.)
- quote_get → get real-time price snapshot (last, OHLC, volume)
- data_get_ohlcv → get price bars. ALWAYS pass summary=true unless you need individual bars

Reading custom Pine indicator output (line.new/label.new/table.new/box.new drawings):
- data_get_pine_lines → horizontal price levels from custom indicators (deduplicated, sorted)
- data_get_pine_labels → text annotations with prices ("PDH 24550", "Bias Long", etc.)
- data_get_pine_tables → table data as formatted rows (session stats, analytics dashboards)
- data_get_pine_boxes → price zones as {high, low} pairs
- ALWAYS pass study_filter to target a specific indicator by name (e.g., study_filter="Profiler")
- Indicators must be VISIBLE on chart for these to work

Changing the chart:
- chart_set_symbol, chart_set_timeframe, chart_set_type → change ticker/resolution/style
- chart_manage_indicator → add/remove studies. USE FULL NAMES: "Relative Strength Index" not "RSI"
- chart_scroll_to_date → jump to a date (ISO format)
- indicator_set_inputs → change indicator settings (length, source, etc.)

Pine Script development:
- pine_set_source → inject code, pine_smart_compile → compile + check errors
- pine_get_errors → read errors, pine_get_console → read log output
- WARNING: pine_get_source can return 200KB+ for complex scripts — avoid unless editing

Screenshots: capture_screenshot → regions: "full", "chart", "strategy_tester"
Replay: replay_start → replay_step → replay_trade → replay_status → replay_stop
Batch: batch_run → run action across multiple symbols/timeframes
Drawing: draw_shape → horizontal_line, trend_line, rectangle, text
Alerts: alert_create, alert_list, alert_delete
Launch: tv_launch → auto-detect and start TradingView with CDP on any platform
Panes: pane_list, pane_set_layout (s, 2h, 2v, 4, 6, 8), pane_focus, pane_set_symbol
Tabs: tab_list, tab_new, tab_close, tab_switch

CONTEXT MANAGEMENT:
- ALWAYS use summary=true on data_get_ohlcv
- ALWAYS use study_filter on pine tools when you know which indicator you want
- NEVER use verbose=true unless user specifically asks for raw data
- Prefer capture_screenshot for visual context over pulling large datasets
- Call chart_get_state ONCE at start, reuse entity IDs

> Owner: Team lead · Read in: every phase · Agent: read-only

## Ask the human (blocking)

Record a decision in `docs/decisions-log.md` (format under "Decision record"), ask, and wait when:

- a technology, version or service from `project/00_setup/tech-stack.md` does not work or needs changing;
- a frozen acceptance test appears wrong (only a human may update the manifest afterwards);
- a Critical or High finding would be downgraded or accepted.

## Decide and record (non-blocking)

When a requirement allows two behaviours a user would notice, choose the more conservative one, record it as "pending review", and continue.

Also non-blocking, record and continue: a finding listed in project/00_setup/pre-approved.md whose evidence matches (cite its ID, apply its action, do not ask); a pinned tool that runs but reports another version; a scanner analyser disabled for lack of credentials; dev-only tooling added under the `tech-stack.md` rule.

## Decision record

Append each decision to `docs/decisions-log.md` in this format:

```
## D-nn: <short title>
- Timestamp:
- Phase:
- Type: blocking | non-blocking
- Trigger: <what happened; cite IDs and files>
- Options: <numbered alternatives; mark the proposed default>
- Human response: <answer and time, or "none">
- Resolution: <chosen option> | pending review
```

- Never delete or rewrite a record; add a follow-up record instead.
- The phase 7 gate fails while any record lacks a resolution.

## Identifiers

| Prefix | Meaning | Defined in |
|---|---|---|
| `US-nnn` / `AC-nnn-nn` | User story / acceptance criterion | `project/01_requirements/user-stories.md` / `project/01_requirements/acceptance-criteria.md` |
| `BR-nn` / `OQ-nn` | Business rule / open question | `project/01_requirements/` |
| `AR-nn` | Architecture constraint | `project/02_design/architecture.md` |

| `ES-nn` | Engineering standard | `general/engineering-standards.md` |
| `NFR-nn` | Non-functional requirement | `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` |
| `DoD-nn` / `DoD-Pnn` | Done criterion, general / project | `general/quality/` / `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` |
| `F-nn` / `D-nn` | Finding / decision | `docs/06_verification-report.md` / `docs/decisions-log.md` |

Tests, commits and findings reference these IDs.

- Do not squash, rebase or rewrite history.

## Progress

Update `docs/00_progress.md` at every gate and before any stop, so a fresh session can resume.

## Output

- Write command output longer than 50 lines to `out/logs/`; report only a summary and the path.
- Use only the severity levels in `general/quality/severity-scale.md`.

## Secrets (`.env`)

You never need to see a secret value; the tools that run need it, not you.

- Do not read `.env` with a file tool, and do not print, copy or log its values: no `cat`, `echo`, `env`, `printenv` or `docker compose config` on it, in commands, files, logs, commit messages or the conversation.
- Pass values to tools without showing them: `docker compose --env-file .env`, or `export NAME="$(sed -n 's/^NAME=//p' .env | tr -d '\r')"` inside the command that needs it.
- Check presence and emptiness only, as in `general/skills/preflight`.
- Before saving output from a command that may print an environment, filter it so no value is written.
- The phase 6 secret-leak check (`general/skills/verify-release`) must find nothing.

## Statistics

Record with `03_statistics/tools/stat.mjs`, which writes the real clock: `init` once in phase 0; `phase <n> start` and `phase <n> end` at every phase boundary (a start closes the previous phase, `phase 7 end` closes the run); `wait start <cause> "<reason>" [decisionId]` and `wait end` around every wait for the human, including stops and restarts. > Owner: Team lead · Read in: phase 0 · Agent: read-only

If the pin resolves and the tool runs but reports another version (for example an image tag that differs from the tool's own version), record a non-blocking decision and continue. If it does not resolve or run, it is a failure to report.
3. For every environment and service in `environments.md` needed locally: confirm it is running or reachable (container runtime, registries, local substitutes).
4. For every key in `secrets.env.example` not marked test-only or not needed: confirm `.env` (repository root) gives it a non-empty value. Check with `sed -n 's/^KEY=//p' .env | tr -d ' \r"'"'"'' | grep -q .`, not with a hand-written read loop: this also reads a last line without a trailing newline, removes Windows line endings, and treats a value of only quotes or spaces as empty (the loop form skipped the last line in run 04). 5. For every `dependencies` entry: confirm the exact version resolves from its `source`.
6. Scan the listed dependency set with the `dependency-scan` tools from `tooling`, using each tool's `options`; any Critical or High result is a blocking decision. If a default analyser fails because it needs credentials that `secrets.env.example` does not list, disable that analyser, record a non-blocking decision and re-run. The scan must complete with at least one analyser, otherwise it is a failure to report.
7. Confirm the working tree is clean (apart from an untracked `.env` and `03_statistics/run-log.json`, which is created in this phase) and on the intended starting commit.
8. Write `docs/00_input-manifest.sha256`: SHA-256 of every file under `01_input/` and every protected root file (`README.md` sections 1 and 2), LF-normalised, `sha256sum` format.
9. Before reporting any failure, re-run that check a second, different way (for example list the key names in `.env` with values masked, or re-run the version command). Report only failures both checks confirm. Write every result to the report with the method used (never values). Collect all failures a human must fix into one message:
   - missing tools or services: what to install or start, and the exact version;
   - missing secrets: which key to add to `.env` (never ask for the value in the conversation);
   - version or vulnerability problems: the proposed alternatives, as a blocking decision.
10. Wait for the answer, re-run only the failed checks, and repeat until everything passes.

content.content:
# Engineering standards

> Owner: Team lead · Read in: phases 0, 4, 6, 7 · Agent: read-only

Apply to every component of every project.

| ID | Standard |
|---|---|
| ES-01 | Every value that differs between environments comes from configuration; secrets have no default in code. |
| ES-02 | Secrets are never committed; `.env` is ignored by git; `project/00_setup/secrets.env.example` lists every key. |
| ES-03 | The repository has `.gitattributes` normalising text files to LF and `.gitignore` excluding build output, dependencies and local config. |
| ES-04 | Dependency versions are exact and lock files are committed. |
| ES-05 | Each component offers one command each to build, test, check (format, lint, type check) and run; its README lists them. |
| ES-06 | Root README: purpose, components, quick start, documentation map. Component README: prerequisites, configuration (settings and secrets, with source), build, run, test, troubleshooting. |
| ES-07 | Logs contain no secrets or personal data; errors shown to users contain no internal details. |
| ES-08 | Persistent data structures are versioned (migrations or equivalent). |
| ES-09 | Deployable services expose health and readiness information. |
| ES-10 | Changes are limited to the task; do not refactor unrelated code. |
# Security baseline

> Owner: Security officer · Read in: phases 0, 2, 6 · Agent: read-only

Applies to every project. Project requirements (`SR-nn`) and the chosen standard level are in `project/02_design/security-requirements.md`.

## Verification standard by component type

| Component type | Standard | Default level |
|---|---|---|

# Run guide (TDD)

This setup is run three times, once each by kyuhi, tanej and tjan, in one shared environment, and the three runs are compared. Everything below is therefore the same for everyone; the only things that may differ are the four lines in the table "If you are not kyuhi".

## 1. Prepare the run folder (clone, branch, .env)
1. **Clone the template** into a new folder named after the run. The TDD template is the branch `template/tdd` of the shared runs repository (`main` stays the spec-driven template 1.7); you never commit to either. Clone to a short path near the root of a drive (Windows stops at 260 characters in a path, and the run creates deep folders), then open a terminal in the new folder:
   ```bash
   git clone --branch template/tdd https://github.com/SQA-interns/Structured_Input_Files.git kyuhi_single-agent_tdd_v001
   cd kyuhi_single-agent_tdd_v001
   ```
   Use your own operator name in the folder name. Sign in to GitHub when asked.
2. **Create the run's branch** (it is the only branch you work and push on): `<operator>/single-agent/tdd/v001`, for kyuhi `kyuhi/single-agent/tdd/v001`:
   ```bash
   git switch -c kyuhi/single-agent/tdd/v001
   ```
3. **Keep `.env` out of git before you create it** (the template has no `.gitignore`; the agent writes one in phase 0):
   - Git Bash: `echo .env >> .git/info/exclude`
   - PowerShell: `Add-Content -Encoding ascii .git\info\exclude ".env"`
4. **Check `01_input/01_project/00_setup/run-config.md`** (the project inputs are already in the clone, there is nothing to copy).
      - operator `kyuhi`,
      - machine `kyuhiPC`,
      - plan `PRO`,
      - permission mode `auto`,
      - model `claude-opus-5-5`,
      - effort `medium`
      - Run label: **change it for every run** (`kyuhi_single-agent_tdd_v001`, then `v002`,...).
      - Run ID: **keep empty it generates by itself**
      - Starting commit: **keep empty it generates by itself**
5. **Check the price row in `03_statistics/usage.md`.** It is pre-filled for Opus 5.5; change it only if the prices or the model changed.
6. **Create `.env`**: copy `01_input/01_project/00_setup/secrets.env.example` to `.env` in the run folder and fill every value (database password, organizer login, NVD key). Never paste a secret into the chat.
7. **Commit your changes to `run-config.md` (and `usage.md`, if you changed it)** so the starting commit contains the right operator, machine, plan and label: `git add -A`, `git commit -m "run setup <run label>"`. If you changed nothing there is nothing to commit and the starting commit is the commit of `template/tdd` you cloned. Check that `git status` does not list `.env` before anything is pushed.
8. **Push the run's branch** (so the start state is on record before the agent starts; `origin` is already set by the clone):
   ```bash
   git push -u origin kyuhi/single-agent/tdd/v001
   ```
   Use your own operator name in the branch. Every operator pushes to a branch of its own, never to `main`. Do not push before `.env` is confirmed absent from `git status`.
9. **Set the same permission mode** you set in `run-config.md`.
10. **Check the environment** (the same for all three operators): Docker Engine 29.8.1 and Compose 5.5.1, Node 24.13.0, Java 21, internet access for the scanners (NVD key in `.env`), no other heavy load on the machine during the run, one session only.

**If you are not kyuhi**, change only these lines in `01_input/01_project/00_setup/run-config.md` and nothing else (not the inputs, not the tools):

| Line | kyuhi | tanej | tjan |
|---|---|---|---|
| Operator | `kyuhi` | `tanej` | `tjan` |
| Machine | `kyuhiPC` | a label of your computer | a label of your computer |
| Plan | `PRO` | your plan | your plan |
| Run label | `kyuhi_single-agent_tdd_v001` | `tanej_single-agent_tdd_v001` | `tjan_single-agent_tdd_v001` |

## 2. Start the run
Open a **new agent session in the run folder** (only one session per run; do not open other sessions in this folder, the newest one is taken as the run's transcript) and send exactly:

```
Read AGENTS.md and start.
```

## 3. During the run
- Answer tooling and environment questions with the standard answers below, the same way in every run.
- The acceptance criteria, the end-to-end scenarios and the answers to the open questions are inputs, so the agent should not ask about business behaviour. If it does anyway, answer only: *"No further information is available. Choose the proposed default option and record it as a decision."*
- To **any other question not listed below**, give the same answer in every run: *"Choose the proposed default option and record it as a decision."* A frozen acceptance test that cannot pass (a defect in the test harness or in one assertion): approve the agent's proposed default fix (option 1). Do not add your own ideas or hints; different answers make the runs incomparable.
- The agent works until the **quality gate** is met (mutation score 90 %, line coverage 95 %, per component). Do not tell it to stop earlier or to go further.
- Type at least one line of each answer yourself; a pasted-only answer makes the agent ask you to confirm.
- Do not change the input files. Do not leave a question unanswered for more than an hour: the cache expires and the wait is excluded from the results, but the time is lost. If you must stop, tell the agent so it records the wait.

**Standard answers (conference registration project; decision numbers differ, recognise them by subject)**
| Phase | The agent asks about | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Host JDK, Node, npm or Docker differs from the pins by a patch version | No question: pre-approved (PA-05). Anything else (a different minor or major version): approve the installed version only if the agent says everything runs. |
| 0 | `vitest` or `jscpd` has Critical or High vulnerabilities | Move to the fixed versions the agent proposes (`jscpd` 5.4.0). `vitest` and `@vitest/coverage-v8` stay on 4.1.11: 5.x does not work with Stryker (see phase 6). No question if `tech-stack.md` already has them. |
| 0 | CVE-2025-7962 on `angus-activation`, CVE-2025-15104 on `hibernate-validator`, dev-only `npm audit` advisories | No question: pre-approved in `01_project/00_setup/pre-approved.md` (PA-01 to PA-03). If the agent asks anyway, answer: *use pre-approved.md*. |
| 6 | Semgrep "basic authentication" (High) on the organizer endpoint | No question: pre-approved (PA-04). If the agent asks anyway, answer: *use pre-approved.md*. |
| 4 | A red test does not compile because the class or function does not exist yet | No question: stubs that report "not implemented" go into the `test:` commit (`working-rules.md`, Commits). If the agent asks anyway, answer: *use the rule in working-rules.md*. |
| 4 | Whether several acceptance criteria may share one cycle | No question: a range of ACs of one story with one code path is allowed (`phases.md`, "TDD cycle"). If the agent asks anyway, answer: *use the rule in phases.md*. |
| 4 | A frozen acceptance test cannot pass with a correct implementation | Approve the agent's proposed default fix (option 1), as in section 3. |
| 5, 6 | Stryker reports an implausibly low frontend score (about 25 %) or the agent says mutants are not activated | Approve `vitest` and `@vitest/coverage-v8` 4.1.x, the same version for both; `@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner` 10.0.0 does not work with Vitest 5. No question if `tech-stack.md` has 4.1.11. |

Anything the agent decides on its own (for example a scanner false positive rated Medium) needs no answer.

## 4. After the run
The measuring is automatic and nothing is typed or copied by hand: cost, tokens, times, context, approval prompts and commits are all calculated from the session transcript and git. `.claude/settings.json` in the run folder holds two hooks that build the report: the Stop hook does it about 8 seconds after the agent's last reply once the run has ended (the agent has written the end time with `stat.mjs phase 7 end`), and the SessionEnd hook repeats it when you close the session. Do not edit or delete the file. If Claude Code asks whether to trust the folder or its hooks, accept.
1. **Wait for the agent's final message, then about 30 seconds.** You do not need to close the session. Check that `03_statistics/results/run-report.html` exists; the hook has then written `03_statistics/results/` (report, measurements, usage summary, commits, readable transcript) and `03_statistics/data/` (transcript backup), and filled the Run, Time, Commits and Cost sections of `03_statistics/run-summary.md`. `03_statistics/results/auto-report.log` shows what it did. Closing the session with `/exit` is optional: it only repeats the build from the final transcript.
# Metrics

> Owner: Experiment lead · Read in: every phase and post-run · Agent: read-only

Experiment measurement only. Record observed values; never estimate. An unobservable value stays `null` with a `<field>Reason`.

Goal column: **↓** lower is better, **↑** higher is better, **=** should equal the stated value, **i** information for interpreting other numbers.

## Principles

- **Human waiting is not part of the result.** Agent time is wall time minus every wait for a human. A wait over one hour also lets the 1-hour prompt cache expire, and the call after it writes the whole context again; that rebuild is a cost of the wait, so `usage.costUsdExclWaits` removes it. Compare runs on agent time and `costUsdExclWaits`.
- **Record only what only you can see, and with the clock tool.** The agent records what happened (waits, loops, decisions, deviations, test and quality results). Timestamps come from `tools/stat.mjs`, never from memory or estimates. Everything that can be computed from the transcripts and git is computed after the run by `tools/build-report.mjs`, so the run spends no calls on it.
- **Make runs comparable.** Say what a number covers. Scope, level and tool of coverage, mutation score and code size are defined in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`.

## 1. Agent, during the run → `run-log.json`

Phase 0, first action: `node 03_statistics/tools/stat.mjs init`. It creates `run-log.json` from the template, a unique `runId`, the start time and commit, the transcript path and the environment. It prints what it wrote.

| Field | When | How | Goal |
|---|---|---|---|
| `runId`, `model`, `effort`, `templateVersion`, `start`, `startCommit`, `transcript`, `environment` | phase 0 | written by `stat.mjs init` from `run-config.md`, git and the host | i |
| `phases[].start`, `phases[].end` | every phase boundary | `stat.mjs phase <n> start` and `stat.mjs phase <n> end`; a start also closes the previous phase, `phase 7 end` also sets `end` and `finalCommit` | ↓ agent time per phase |
| `humanInterventions[]` | every time the agent waits for the human or the human acts, including stops, restarts and installs | `stat.mjs wait start <cause> "<reason>" [decisionId]` when you ask or stop, `stat.mjs wait end` when work resumes. `cause`: `decision`, `environment`, `approval`, `session`, `other` | ↓ count and minutes; every minute here is excluded from agent time |
| `firstTestRun`, `finalTestRun` | first full run before fixes (start of phase 5, after the TDD build); last full run | edit the file: `passed`, `failed` and `byLevel` (`unit`, `integration`, `acceptance`, `architecture`, `e2e` counts) | first: ↓ failed (defects the first run found); final: ↑ passed, `failed` = 0 |
| `acceptanceCriteria` | end of phase 3; changes in phase 4 | `total` criteria, `frozenTests`, `frozenTestChanges[]` as `{decisionId, reason}` | ↑ criteria covered by tests; ↓ frozen-test changes (each one needed a human) |
| `findings` | end of phase 6 | counts by severity, as found | ↓ |
| `openAtEnd` | end of phase 6 | Critical, High and Medium findings still open after triage | = 0 for Critical and High |
| `fixLoops[]` | each verify → fix → re-verify loop | `{loop, findings, category, needsHuman, change, start, end}`. `category`: `test-gap`, `security-config`, `dependency`, `defect`, `process`, `tooling`. `start` is the first fix action, `end` the clean re-check (UTC, `date -u +%FT%TZ`) | ↓ minutes per loop; a loop that repeats across runs belongs in the template |

This setup is run three times, once each by kyuhi, tanej and tjan, in one shared environment, and the three runs are compared. Everything below is therefore the same for everyone; the only things that may differ are the four lines in the table "If you are not kyuhi".

   git clone --branch template/tdd https://github.com/SQA-interns/Structured_Input_Files.git kyuhi_single-agent_tdd_v001

   ```

   ```

content.content:
# Quality requirements

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phases 2, 6, 7 · Agent: read-only

Adds to `general/quality/` (definition of done, test strategy, severity scale); do not repeat those here.

## Non-functional requirements

| ID | Category (performance, availability, accessibility, localisation, usability, …) | Requirement | How it is checked |
|---|---|---|---|
| NFR-01 | Localisation | Names and other text with Slovenian characters (č, š, ž) survive the form, database, JSON copy, emails and Excel export unchanged. | an end-to-end test with such input |
| NFR-02 | Reliability | Stored registrations and JSON copies survive recreation of every container. | runtime demonstration: `docker compose down` then `up`, data still present |
| NFR-03 | Usability | The frontend validates fields before submission and shows the backend's field errors next to the fields. | component tests |
| NFR-04 | Availability | The backend reports health and readiness, and the containers use them in health checks. | runtime demonstration |

## Thresholds

These thresholds are the **quality gate** of the project: the same in every run, per component (backend, frontend), over the scope and with the tests defined in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`. The agent works until each component meets them, then stops adding tests for that component (rules and stop rule: "Quality gate" in `measurement-scope.md`). The rows below are read by `tools/build-report.mjs`; keep the format `>= <number> %`.

| Measure | Threshold |
|---|---|
| Line coverage (all levels together) | >= 95 % |
| Mutation score (adjusted) | >= 90 % |
| Branch coverage | record only |

## Mutation scope

The paths or packages whose code is mutated, the same in every run of this project (default: all production code of the component). Selection rule: validation, security, persistence and business-rule code. Rules: `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`.

| Component | Paths or packages | Exclusions and reason |
|---|---|---|
| backend | `si.konferenca.registration.**` (all production code under the root package, including validation, security, persistence, business-rule, mail and export code) | The `@SpringBootApplication` entry-point class (no logic); generated code. Nothing else may be excluded. |
| frontend | `src/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx,vue}` (all production source of the frontend) | Test files, type-declaration files (`*.d.ts`), the bootstrap file that only mounts the app, generated code. Nothing else may be excluded. |

The scope is all production code of both components, so mutation scores are on the same basis in every run. It is the root package and the source folder, not a list of sub-packages, because the agent chooses the sub-packages in phase 2. Each component's full automated suite runs against it (`measurement-scope.md`, "Mutation score").

## Additional done criteria

| ID | Criterion | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| DoD-P01 | Against the running local stack: one external and one student registration succeed. | runtime demonstration log |
| DoD-P02 | Each registration is in PostgreSQL and has its JSON copy. | database query, file listing |
| DoD-P03 | The participant email and the organizer email (with the JSON attachment) arrive in Mailpit. | Mailpit API output |
| DoD-P04 | The organizer downloads a valid Excel workbook; the same request without organizer access is refused. | response codes, opened workbook |
| DoD-P05 | The production reCAPTCHA code path is tested against a mocked verification endpoint, including a rejected token. | test report |

## Overrides

None.
# Measurement scope

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phases 3, 5, 6 · Agent: read-only

Defines what test counts, coverage, mutation score and code size mean, so that figures from different runs compare. Record every figure in `run-log.json` → `codeMetrics` and in `docs/06_verification-report.md` with its scope, level and tool. The project selects paths and exclusions in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` ("Mutation scope"); this file never names them.

## Constraints

- Do not change a tool's scope, filters, exclusions or thresholds to improve a number. A change is a decision record.
- Do not report a figure without its scope, level and tool.
- Production code is the source a component ships. It excludes tests, generated code, the application entry point and anything listed under "Measurement exclusions" in `docs/03_test-strategy.md` with a reason. Decide the exclusions in phase 3, before any test is written; do not extend them later.
- Test code never counts towards coverage or mutation.

## Test counts

Per component and level (`unit`, `integration`, `acceptance`, `architecture`, `e2e`), passed and failed, from the runner's own report.

## Coverage

Line and branch, per component, as three figures: `unit` (unit tests only), `nonUnit` (integration, acceptance and end-to-end tests that exercise the component) and `all` (one merged report). The headline figure is `all`.

## Mutation score

- **Scope:** all production code of the component, narrowed only to the paths in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` "Mutation scope", which are the same in every run of the project (default: all production code). Do not narrow it by running only some tests or by excluding packages that are not listed there.

# User stories

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 6 · Agent: read-only

## Format

- Stories: `US-nnn`, "As a … I want … so that …", plus in-scope and out-of-scope notes.
- Acceptance criteria are given in `acceptance-criteria.md` as `AC-nnn-nn` (Given/When/Then), one observable behaviour each, each citing its `US` and any `BR`; the agent does not derive them.
- Do not invent behaviour a story does not state; record the gap as an `OQ` in `scope.md`.

## Stories

Epic: as a conference organizer, I want participants to register online, so that registrations are collected and managed reliably.

### US-001 External participant registration

As an external participant, I want to register using the external participant form, so that I can attend the conference and the activities I select.
In scope: the external form (BR-01), selecting active options (BR-04). Out of scope: payment, accounts, editing a submitted registration.

### US-002 Student registration

As a student, I want to register using the student form, so that I can attend the conference and the activities available to students.
In scope: the student form (BR-01), selecting active options (BR-04). Out of scope: verifying student status externally, accounts.

### US-003 Configurable conference options

As an organizer, I want workshops, events, meals and other optional activities to be configurable, so that the system can be reused when the programme changes.
Out of scope: an administration UI for options.

### US-004 Registration confirmation

As a participant, I want a clear confirmation in the application after my registration is processed, so that I know it was received (BR-06).

### US-005 Reliable registration storage

As an organizer, I want every accepted registration stored reliably, so that none is lost and each can be recovered (BR-07).

### US-006 Participant email confirmation

As a participant, I want an email confirming my registration, so that I have a record of it.

### US-007 Organizer notification

As an organizer, I want an email when someone registers, containing the submitted data with the raw registration JSON attached, so that I can monitor incoming registrations.

### US-008 Registration export

As an organizer, I want to export the current registrations as an Excel workbook, so that I can process them outside the system (BR-08).
# Business rules

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 6 · Agent: read-only

## Rules

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| BR-01 | There are two registration types: external participant and student. Each has the fixed fields listed under Data; configuration never changes them. |
| BR-02 | Required fields are never empty; leading and trailing whitespace is not significant. |
| BR-03 | Email has a valid email format. Text accepts Unicode, including Slovenian characters (č, š, ž). |
| BR-04 | Options are grouped as workshops, events, meals and other activities. Only active options can be selected; unknown or inactive options are rejected. |
| BR-05 | Mandatory consents must be given and are never preselected. |
| BR-06 | The in-application confirmation is shown only after the registration was accepted. |
| BR-07 | An accepted registration is stored in the database and as a raw JSON copy on persistent storage. |
| BR-08 | Only organizers can obtain the registration list; it is not reachable without organizer access. |

## Data

| Form or entity | Fields (all required) |
|---|---|
| External participant | first name, last name, email, organization / institution |
| Student | first name, last name, email, study institution, study programme, student ID |
| Conference option | stable identifier, display name, category (workshop, event, meal, other), active or inactive |
| Consent | which consents exist and their wording: `OQ-02` |

## Glossary

- Participant: a person who registers, external or student.
- Organizer: conference staff who receive notifications and export registrations.
- Option: a selectable workshop, event, meal or other activity.
- Active option: an option currently offered for selection.
- Raw JSON copy: the registration exactly as accepted, stored as a file for backup.
 Kept until the operator deletes them; no automatic deletion. The release notes tell the operator to delete the database rows and JSON copies no later than 12 months after the conference. |Allowed; each registration is stored separately and the export shows both. |No limit per category; each option at most once per registration, duplicates are rejected. |The registration stays accepted (HTTP 201, confirmation shown). Emails are sent only after the database row and the JSON copy exist; an email failure is logged with the registration id only, no personal data. |Consents are part of the conference configuration (id, wording, mandatory). The shipped configuration has one mandatory consent `privacy`: "I agree that my personal data is processed for organizing the conference and that it is shared with the conference organizers." |Every option carries a configured list of registration types it is available to (default: both); the backend rejects an option that is not available to the registration type. |# Scope

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 6 · Agent: read-only

## In scope

- Registration forms for external participants and students (US-001, US-002)
- Configurable conference options (US-003)
- In-application confirmation, participant confirmation email, organizer notification email with the JSON attachment (US-004, US-006, US-007)
- Storage in the database plus a raw JSON copy (US-005)
- Excel export for organizers (US-008)
- Anti-automation protection of the registration form

## Out of scope

- Participant accounts and login
- Payment processing
- Editing or cancelling a submitted registration
- Verifying student status externally
- An administration UI or dashboard, including option configuration
- Integration with an identity provider

## Priorities

1. A registration is never lost: storage (BR-07) comes before any notification.
2. Security and privacy (`project/02_design/security-requirements.md`) come before convenience.
3. The participant flow (US-001 to US-006) comes before organizer features (US-007, US-008).

## Open questions

| ID | Question | Owner | Answer |
|---|---|---|---|
| OQ-01 | Are all options available to students, or are some only for external participants? | Product owner | Every option carries a configured list of registration types it is available to (default: both); the backend rejects an option that is not available to the registration type. |
| OQ-02 | Which mandatory consents exist, and what is their wording? | Product owner | Consents are part of the conference configuration (id, wording, mandatory). The shipped configuration has one mandatory consent `privacy`: "I agree that my personal data is processed for organizing the conference and that it is shared with the conference organizers." |
| OQ-03 | What happens when storage succeeds but an email fails? | Product owner | The registration stays accepted (HTTP 201, confirmation shown). Emails are sent only after the database row and the JSON copy exist; an email failure is logged with the registration id only, no personal data. |
| OQ-04 | How many options may a participant select per category? | Product owner | No limit per category; each option at most once per registration, duplicates are rejected. |
| OQ-05 | Is a second registration with the same email allowed? | Product owner | Allowed; each registration is stored separately and the export shows both. |
| OQ-06 | How long are registrations and JSON copies kept? | Product owner | Kept until the operator deletes them; no automatic deletion. The release notes tell the operator to delete the database rows and JSON copies no later than 12 months after the conference. |

The answers are the product owner's decisions and hold for every run of this project; the agent records no decision for them. A new question that arises later becomes a decision record as usual.

content.content:
# Acceptance criteria

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 3, 6 · Agent: read-only

This list is an input, the same in every run of this project: the agent does not derive, add, merge or reword criteria. Each criterion states one observable behaviour (Given / When / Then) and cites its story and rules. "Rejected" always means: the API answers with an error status and field errors, no database row and no JSON copy are created, and no email is sent. The open questions are answered in `scope.md` (OQ-01 to OQ-06).

Common terms used below:

- *valid external submission*: registration type `EXTERNAL`; first name, last name, email, organization filled; every mandatory consent given; a reCAPTCHA token the verifier accepts; zero or more distinct active option ids available to the type.
- *valid student submission*: as above with type `STUDENT` and study institution, study programme and student ID instead of organization.

## US-001 External participant registration

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-001-01 | Given active options are configured, when a valid external submission is sent, then it is accepted (HTTP 201) and the response contains the new registration id. | BR-01, BR-04 |
| AC-001-02 | Given the external form, when any one required field (first name, last name, email, organization) is missing, empty or only whitespace, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that field. | BR-01, BR-02 |
| AC-001-03 | Given a valid external submission whose text fields have leading and trailing spaces, when it is accepted, then the stored values have the spaces removed. | BR-02 |
| AC-001-04 | Given the external form, when the email does not have a valid email format, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for the email field. | BR-03 |
| AC-001-05 | Given the external form, when an option id is unknown, inactive or listed twice, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for the options. | BR-04, SR-04, OQ-04 |
| AC-001-06 | Given the external form, when a mandatory consent is not given, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that consent. | BR-05, OQ-02 |
| AC-001-07 | Given the external form, when the reCAPTCHA token is missing or the verifier rejects it, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) and nothing is stored. | SR-01, scope (anti-automation) |
| AC-001-08 | Given the registration page, when the participant chooses "external participant", then the page shows exactly the external fields, the active options grouped as workshops, events, meals and other activities, and every consent checkbox unchecked. | BR-01, BR-04, BR-05 |

## US-002 Student registration

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-002-01 | Given active options are configured, when a valid student submission is sent, then it is accepted (HTTP 201) and the response contains the new registration id. | BR-01, BR-04 |
| AC-002-02 | Given the student form, when any one required field (first name, last name, email, study institution, study programme, student ID) is missing, empty or only whitespace, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that field. | BR-01, BR-02 |
| AC-002-03 | Given the student form, when the email does not have a valid email format, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for the email field. | BR-03 |
| AC-002-04 | Given an active option configured as not available to students, when a student submission selects it, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for the options. | BR-04, OQ-01 |
| AC-002-05 | Given the student form, when a mandatory consent is not given, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that consent. | BR-05, OQ-02 |
| AC-002-06 | Given the student form, when the reCAPTCHA token is missing or the verifier rejects it, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) and nothing is stored. | SR-01 |
| AC-002-07 | Given the registration page, when the participant chooses "student", then the page shows exactly the student fields and only the active options available to students, grouped by category, with every consent checkbox unchecked. | BR-01, BR-04, BR-05, OQ-01 |

## US-003 Configurable conference options

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-003-01 | Given a configuration with active and inactive options, when the form configuration is requested, then it lists only the active options, each with its identifier, display name, category and the registration types it is available to. | BR-04 |
| AC-003-02 | Given the backend is started with a different options configuration (an option added, one deactivated), when the form configuration is requested, then it reflects the new configuration, with no code change. | AR-04 |
| AC-003-03 | Given an options configuration that is invalid (duplicate identifier, unknown category, missing name), when the backend starts, then it refuses to start. | AR-04 |

## US-004 Registration confirmation

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-004-01 | Given a filled form, when the backend accepts the registration, then the page shows a confirmation with the participant's name and the selected options, and the form is no longer shown. | BR-06 |
| AC-004-02 | Given a filled form, when the backend rejects the registration with field errors, then no confirmation is shown, each error is shown next to its field, and the entered values remain. | BR-06, NFR-03 |
| AC-004-03 | Given a form with an empty required field or an invalid email, when the participant submits, then the page shows the field errors and sends no request to the backend. | NFR-03 |
| AC-004-04 | Given a filled form, when the backend fails or cannot be reached, then no confirmation is shown and a general error message without technical details is shown. | BR-06, SB-07 |

## US-005 Reliable registration storage

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-005-01 | Given a valid submission, when it is accepted, then the database holds one registration with the type, every submitted field, the selected options, each consent with the time it was given, and the time of registration. | BR-07 |
| AC-005-02 | Given a valid submission, when it is accepted, then a JSON copy named after the registration id exists in the JSON copy directory and contains the registration as accepted. | BR-07 |
| AC-005-03 | Given the JSON copy cannot be written, when a valid submission is sent, then the API answers with an error (not 201) and no registration is left in the database. | BR-07, AR-05 |
| AC-005-04 | Given a valid submission with Slovenian characters (č, š, ž, Č, Š, Ž) in the names and institution, when it is accepted, then the database row and the JSON copy contain the text unchanged. | BR-03, NFR-01 |

## US-006 Participant email confirmation

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-006-01 | Given a valid submission, when it is accepted, then one email is sent to the participant's address naming the conference, the participant and the selected options. | US-006 |
| AC-006-02 | Given a submission whose text fields contain line breaks, header-like text or HTML markup, when the confirmation email is sent, then the email has no additional headers or recipients and the markup appears only as literal text. | SR-05 |
| AC-006-03 | Given the mail server is unavailable, when a valid submission is sent, then the registration is still accepted (HTTP 201) and stored. | OQ-03, OQ-03 |

## US-007 Organizer notification

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-007-01 | Given organizer addresses are configured, when a registration is accepted, then each organizer address receives a notification email containing the submitted registration data. | US-007 |
| AC-007-02 | Given a registration is accepted, when the organizer notification is sent, then it has a JSON attachment whose content equals the stored JSON copy. | US-007, BR-07, SR-07 |

## US-008 Registration export

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-008-01 | Given stored registrations, when an organizer requests the export with valid organizer credentials, then the response is an Excel workbook (`.xlsx`) with one row per registration, containing its type, fields, selected options, consents and registration time. | BR-08 |
| AC-008-02 | Given stored registrations, when the export is requested without credentials or with wrong credentials, then it is refused (HTTP 401) and no registration data is returned. | BR-08, SB-02 |
| AC-008-03 | Given a registration with Slovenian characters, when the organizer exports, then the workbook cell contains the text unchanged. | NFR-01 |
| AC-008-04 | Given organizer HTTPS-only access is on, when the export is requested with valid credentials over plain HTTP from a client that is not on localhost, then it is refused and no registration data is returned. | SR-06 |

## Traceability

| Story | Criteria |
|---|---|
| US-001 | AC-001-01 … AC-001-08 |
| US-002 | AC-002-01 … AC-002-07 |
| US-003 | AC-003-01 … AC-003-03 |
| US-004 | AC-004-01 … AC-004-04 |
| US-005 | AC-005-01 … AC-005-04 |
| US-006 | AC-006-01 … AC-006-03 |
| US-007 | AC-007-01, AC-007-02 |
| US-008 | AC-008-01 … AC-008-04 |

Total: 35 criteria.

Requirements without their own criterion, covered in the specification and verified in phase 6: SR-03 rate and size limits, NFR-02 persistence across container recreation, NFR-04 health and readiness (runtime demonstration).
# End-to-end scenarios

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 3, 6 · Agent: read-only

The end-to-end tests of this project: exactly one test per scenario below, run against the real local stack (`docker compose up`: frontend, backend, PostgreSQL, Mailpit) through the browser, and the same in every run of this project. The agent writes no other end-to-end test and no scenario is merged or split. Each scenario names the criteria it demonstrates; the acceptance tests (one or more per criterion) carry the detailed cases, so an end-to-end test checks the journey once and does not repeat them.

| ID | Scenario | Steps and observations | Covers |
|---|---|---|---|
| E2E-01 | External participant registers | Open the page, choose "external participant", fill the form with valid data, select at least one option per category, submit. The page shows the confirmation. > Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 3, 6 · Agent: read-only

This list is an input, the same in every run of this project: the agent does not derive, add, merge or reword criteria. Each criterion states one observable behaviour (Given / When / Then) and cites its story and rules. "Rejected" always means: the API answers with an error status and field errors, no database row and no JSON copy are created, and no email is sent. The open questions are answered in `scope.md` (OQ-01 to OQ-06).

Common terms used below:

- *valid external submission*: registration type `EXTERNAL`; first name, last name, email, organization filled; every mandatory consent given; a reCAPTCHA token the verifier accepts; zero or more distinct active option ids available to the type.
- *valid student submission*: as above with type `STUDENT` and study institution, study programme and student ID instead of organization.

# Security requirements

> Owner: Security officer · Read in: phases 2, 6 · Agent: read-only

Adds to `general/security/security-baseline.md` (SB-01 … SB-14); do not repeat those here.

## Verification standard

| Component | Standard | Level | Reason if above the default |
|---|---|---|---|
| backend | OWASP ASVS 5.0 | Level 1 | |
| frontend | OWASP ASVS 5.0 | Level 1 | |

Level 1 is a deliberate choice: the only authentication is one organizer role for one export operation, and the personal data is contact and study data, not sensitive data. Where a requirement below is more specific than ASVS, it applies as well.

## Authentication and authorization

- Participants are anonymous; there are no participant accounts.
- One organizer role may export registrations (BR-08). The mechanism is decided in phase 2, using the organizer credentials from `secrets.env.example`; identity providers are out of scope.
- Everything else (options, registration) is public but protected by SR-01 and SR-03.

## Personal data

| Data item | Purpose | Retention | Shown/exported to |
|---|---|---|---|
| First and last name | identify the participant | `OQ-06` | organizers (email, export) |
| Email | confirmation and contact | `OQ-06` | participant, organizers |
| Organization / institution | attendance records | `OQ-06` | organizers |
| Study institution, programme, student ID | student registration | `OQ-06` | organizers |
| Selected options | plan workshops, events and meals | `OQ-06` | participant (confirmation), organizers |
| Consents given, with timestamp | proof of consent (SB-14) | `OQ-06` | organizers |

## Project requirements

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SR-01 | Every registration is protected by Google reCAPTCHA v2 and verified on the backend; the frontend check alone is never enough. |
| SR-02 | reCAPTCHA test mode is enabled only by environment configuration, never by default; production refuses to start with test mode on or with empty keys. |
| SR-03 | Every public `/api` endpoint (form configuration, registration, export) is rate limited per client, and request bodies have a size limit. |
| SR-04 | Option identifiers are checked against the active configured set (BR-04). |
| SR-05 | Email content is generated safely: user input cannot inject headers or markup. |
| SR-06 | Organizer credentials are never accepted over plain HTTP, except on localhost. |
| SR-07 | The export and the organizer email expose only registration data, never internal fields or other system data. |
| SR-08 | The reverse proxy in front of the backend never forwards a client-supplied `Host` header; it sets the upstream host itself. |

## Overrides

None.
# Definition of Done

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phases 6, 7 · Agent: read-only

Applies to every project; project additions are `DoD-Pnn` in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md`.
Each item needs evidence in `docs/06_verification-report.md`.

| ID | Criterion | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| DoD-01 | The full test suite passes; frozen test hashes match the manifest | test report, hash check |
| DoD-02 | Format, lint, type check and static analysis report no errors | tool output |
| DoD-03 | The quality gate of `general/quality/measurement-scope.md` ("Quality gate") is met for each component, or the shortfall after the third survivor round is recorded with a decision | coverage and mutation reports with scope, raw and adjusted score, rounds |
| DoD-04 | Architecture constraints (`AR`) are checked automatically where possible; no dependency cycles | architecture test output |
| DoD-05 | No open Critical or High finding from the security review and scanners | `general/skills/verify-release` output |
| DoD-06 | Every component runs in its target environment and the core user flows work at runtime, not only in tests | runtime demonstration log |
| DoD-07 | Every AC traces to at least one test and one commit | traceability table |
| DoD-08 | Root and component READMEs (ES-06) work when followed from a clean checkout | clone log |
| DoD-09 | Release notes list everything a human must test manually | `docs/release-notes.md` |
| DoD-10 | Every decision has a resolution or is listed as pending review; inputs and protected files are unchanged | decisions log, `docs/00_input-manifest.sha256` check |
| DoD-11 | The evidence checks in `general/phases.md` hold | `general/phases.md`, "Evidence" |
| DoD-12 | Every AC was built test-first: a `test:` commit naming it precedes its first `feat:` commit, and its red run is logged | `trace-ac.mjs` output (order column), `out/logs/tdd/` |
# Test strategy

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: every phase that writes or runs tests · Agent: read-only

When each test level is written and whether it is frozen is defined in `general/phases.md`. Project thresholds are in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md`.

## Constraints

- Do not test acceptance behaviour through internals; use the component's public interface (API, UI, CLI, messages).
- Do not depend on live external services in automated tests; use the local substitutes in `project/00_setup/environments.md` and list the real services in the release notes for manual testing.
- Do not leave flaky, skipped or disabled tests; fix them or record a decision.
- Do not weaken an assertion to make an incorrect implementation pass.
- Test names contain the AC id they verify.
- Do not count a red step that fails because of a compile, build or harness error; a red test fails on an assertion or on a stub that reports "not implemented".
- Do not commit the code of a TDD cycle before its failing tests are committed (`general/phases.md`, "TDD cycle").

## First complete run

The first complete run is the first full run of every level at the start of phase 5, after the TDD build. Record its result before fixing anything, then classify each failure:

| Class | Action |
|---|---|
| Implementation defect | fix the code |
| Defect in a non-frozen test | fix the test and say so in `docs/03_test-strategy.md` |
| Frozen test appears wrong | blocking decision; do not touch the test |

## Measures (recorded in every project)

Test counts, coverage, mutation score and code size are defined in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`: what each covers, at which level and with which tool.

## Manifest

`docs/03_acceptance-manifest.sha256` uses `sha256sum` format with paths relative to `02_output/`, hashed after LF normalisation.

---
name: write-acceptance-tests
description: Write and freeze the black-box acceptance tests from the given acceptance criteria and end-to-end scenarios and the contracts, before any production code exists (phase 3).
---

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phase 3 · Agent: read-only

- Reads: `project/01_requirements/acceptance-criteria.md`, `project/01_requirements/e2e-scenarios.md`, `docs/02_contracts/`, `general/quality/test-strategy.md`, `general/phases.md`
- Writes: acceptance and end-to-end tests, `docs/03_acceptance-manifest.sha256`, `docs/03_test-strategy.md`
- Does not read: production source code

## Procedure

1. For every AC, write at least one test through the component's public interface that checks the observable outcome the AC states. For a rejection AC, also check that nothing changed. For every scenario in `e2e-scenarios.md`, write exactly one end-to-end test; write no other end-to-end test, and do not split or merge scenarios.
2. Put the AC id in each test name.
3. Run the suite. Every test must fail because the behaviour is missing, not because of a build, configuration or harness error; a test that passes only on bootstrap code is listed in step 4. Fix the harness until that holds.
4. Record the run (pass/fail counts and a one-line reason per group of failures) in `docs/03_test-strategy.md`.
5. Self-check every assertion and helper before the freeze, because a defective frozen test costs a blocking decision: confirm that a correct implementation can make it pass, and that it cannot pass or fail for the wrong reason. Check what each helper returns and what each matcher compares (known cases: the PostgreSQL JDBC driver returns java.sql.Timestamp, not OffsetDateTime, for 	imestamptz unless the type is requested; AssertJ doesNotContain on a  yte[] tests single bytes, not a byte sequence, so compare the first bytes with Arrays.copyOf instead). A test must not contradict another assertion in the same test.
6. Format and lint the tests now; after freezing they cannot change.
7. Commit the tests story by story as you finish them. Then write the manifest (normalised line endings) and commit it alone as the freeze commit.
---
name: tdd-cycle
description: Build the system by red-green-refactor cycles, one acceptance criterion or one range of criteria at a time, until the frozen acceptance and end-to-end tests pass (phase 4).

# Email contract (SMTP)

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: US-006, US-007, SR-05, SR-07, OQ-03 · Agent: writes

Both emails are sent only after the registration transaction committed (database row and JSON copy exist), asynchronously, at most 10 seconds after the 201 response in the test and local environments. A send failure is logged with the registration id only and never changes the response (OQ-03, AC-006-03).

Common to both: `From` = `MAIL_FROM`; `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8` body (no HTML part, so markup stays literal text, SR-05); headers are built only from configuration and validated addresses, never from free text (no header injection); the only recipients are the ones named below.

## Participant confirmation (AC-006-01, AC-006-02)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| To | the participant's email (exactly one recipient, no Cc/Bcc) |
| Subject | `Registration confirmation - <conferenceName>` |
| Body | contains the conference name, the participant's first and last name, and the display name of every selected option (or `none`) |

## Organizer notification (AC-007-01, AC-007-02)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| To | every address in `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` (comma separated), one message per address |
| Subject | `New registration - <conferenceName>` |
| Body | registration id, type, every submitted field of the type, the selected options and the consents with the time given; no internal or system data (SR-07) |
| Attachment | `registration-<id>.json`, `application/json`, bytes equal to the stored JSON copy |

# Excel export contract

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: US-008, BR-08, SR-07, NFR-01 · Agent: writes

`GET /api/registrations/export` (`openapi.json`) returns an `.xlsx` workbook (Office Open XML) with one sheet named `Registrations`.

- Row 1 is the header; then one row per stored registration, ordered by registration time ascending.
- Every cell is a string cell (no formulas; text starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` is stored as plain text, never evaluated).
- Only registration data, no internal fields (SR-07).

| Column | Header | Content |
|---|---|---|
| A | Registration ID | UUID |
| B | Type | `EXTERNAL` or `STUDENT` |
| C | Registered at | ISO-8601 UTC instant, as in the JSON copy |
| D | First name | |
| E | Last name | |
| F | Email | |
| G | Organization / institution | empty for students |
| H | Study institution | empty for external participants |
| I | Study programme | empty for external participants |
| J | Student ID | empty for external participants |
| K | Options | selected option ids, in submission order, joined by `, ` (empty when none) |
| L | Consents | `<consentId> (<givenAt>)` per consent, joined by `, ` |

# Registration form contract (UI)

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: AC-001-08, AC-002-07, AC-004-01..04, NFR-03, AR-01, AR-07 · Agent: writes

One page at `/`. The frontend calls only `GET /api/form-config` and `POST /api/registrations` (`openapi.json`, AR-01). UI text is English (D-08). Accessible names below are exact; tests find elements by role and accessible name.

## Elements

| Element | Role and accessible name |
|---|---|
| Registration type | radio group `Registration type` with radios `External participant` and `Student`; none selected at first; the form fields appear after a choice |
| External fields | textboxes `First name`, `Last name`, `Email`, `Organization / institution` |
| Student fields | textboxes `First name`, `Last name`, `Email`, `Study institution`, `Study programme`, `Student ID` |
| Options | one group (`fieldset`) per category that has at least one option for the chosen type, legends `Workshops`, `Events`, `Meals`, `Other activities`, in that order; one checkbox per active option available to the chosen type, named by its display name; none checked |
| Consents | one checkbox per configured consent, named by its text; never preselected |
| reCAPTCHA | test mode (`recaptcha.testMode`): a checkbox `I am not a robot (test mode)` that yields the token `test-pass` when checked; otherwise the Google reCAPTCHA v2 widget with `recaptcha.siteKey` (the only key in the frontend, AR-07) |
| Submit | button `Register` |

Only the fields of the chosen type are shown (no other textboxes).

## Validation and errors (NFR-03)

- Before sending, the page checks every required field of the type (non-blank after trimming), the email format, and the mandatory consents; with any error it sends no request.
- A field error is shown in an element with id `error-<field>` placed directly after its input, and the input has `aria-invalid="true"` and `aria-describedby="error-<field>"`. `<field>` uses the API field names (`firstName`, …, `optionIds`, `consents.<id>`, `recaptchaToken`); for `optionIds` and `consents.<id>` the described element is the options group or the consent checkbox.
- Backend field errors (400) are shown the same way; entered values remain.
- Any other failure (other status, network error) shows an element with role `alert` and the text `Registration could not be completed. Please try again later.` and no technical details; the form and values remain.

## Confirmation (AC-004-01)

After a 201 response the form is removed and an element with role `status` shows the heading `Registration received`, the participant's first and last name, and a list of the display names of the selected options.

# Configuration contract (backend environment)

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: `project/00_setup/environments.md`, `secrets.env.example`, ES-01, SR-02, SR-03, SR-06 · Agent: writes

Spring relaxed binding: each variable may also be given as the property in the second column. A setting without a default must be provided; the backend refuses to start without it.

| Variable | Property | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `APP_ENVIRONMENT` | `app.environment` | `production` | `production`, `local` or `test`. Production refuses to start when reCAPTCHA test mode is on or a reCAPTCHA key is empty (SR-02) |
| `SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL`, `SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME` | `spring.datasource.*` | none | |
| `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | `spring.datasource.password` | none | secret |
| `MAIL_HOST`, `MAIL_PORT` | `spring.mail.host`, `spring.mail.port` | none | |
| `MAIL_TLS` | `app.mail.tls` | `true` | STARTTLS required when true; local and test set false (Mailpit) |
| `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` | `spring.mail.username`, `spring.mail.password` | empty | secret; production only |
| `MAIL_FROM` | `app.mail.from` | `registration@konferenca.si` | |
| `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` | `app.organizer.emails` | none | comma separated |
| `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` | `app.organizer.username`, `app.organizer.password` | none | secret; password hashed with BCrypt at startup, the plain value is not kept |
| `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY` | `app.organizer.https-only` | `true` | may be false only on local plain HTTP (SR-06) |
| `CONFERENCE_CONFIG_FILE` | `app.conference.config-file` | none | path of the JSON file (`conference-config.schema.json`) |
| `JSON_COPY_DIR` | `app.json-copy.dir` | `/data/registrations` | persistent volume |
| `RECAPTCHA_TEST_MODE` | `app.recaptcha.test-mode` | `false` | test mode accepts only the token `test-pass` and makes no network call |
| `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` | `app.recaptcha.site-key`, `app.recaptcha.secret-key` | empty | secret key never leaves the backend |
| `RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` | `app.recaptcha.verify-url` | `https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify` | tests point it at a mock endpoint (DoD-P05) |
| `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN` | `app.cors.allowed-origin` | empty (no CORS) | local only |
| `RATE_LIMIT_FORM_CONFIG_PER_MINUTE` | `app.rate-limit.form-config-per-minute` | `60` | per client address (SR-03) |
| `RATE_LIMIT_REGISTRATION_PER_MINUTE` | `app.rate-limit.registration-per-minute` | `10` | |
| `RATE_LIMIT_EXPORT_PER_MINUTE` | `app.rate-limit.export-per-minute` | `10` | counts failed logins too (SB-06) |
| `MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` | `app.max-request-bytes` | `16384` | larger bodies get 413 |

The client address is the TCP peer, or the `X-Forwarded-For` value set by a trusted proxy (Tomcat RemoteIpValve, internal address ranges only; `server.forward-headers-strategy=native`).

Health and readiness (ES-09, NFR-04): `/actuator/health/liveness` and `/actuator/health/readiness` on the backend port; not under `/api`, so the reverse proxy does not publish them.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| To | the participant's email (exactly one recipient, no Cc/Bcc) |

| Body | contains the conference name, the participant's first and last name, and the display name of every selected option (or `none`) |

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| To | every address in `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` (comma separated), one message per address |

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: AC-001-08, AC-002-07, AC-004-01..04, NFR-03, AR-01, AR-07 · Agent: writes

One page at `/`. The frontend calls only `GET /api/form-config` and `POST /api/registrations` (`openapi.json`, AR-01). UI text is English (D-08). Accessible names below are exact; tests find elements by role and accessible name.

| Element | Role and accessible name |
|---|---|
| Registration type | radio group `Registration type` with radios `External participant` and `Student`; none selected at first; the form fields appear after a choice |
| External fields | textboxes `First name`, `Last name`, `Email`, `Organization / institution` |
| Student fields | textboxes `First name`, `Last name`, `Email`, `Study institution`, `Study programme`, `Student ID` |
| Options | one group (`fieldset`) per category that has at least one option for the chosen type, legends `Workshops`, `Events`, `Meals`, `Other activities`, in that order; one checkbox per active option available to the chosen type, named by its display name; none checked |
| Consents | one checkbox per configured consent, named by its text; never preselected |

- Before sending, the page checks every required field of the type (non-blank after trimming), the email format, and the mandatory consents; with any error it sends no request.

- Backend field errors (400) are shown the same way; entered values remain.
- Any other failure (other status, network error) shows an element with role `alert` and the text `Registration could not be completed. Please try again later.` and no technical details; the form and values remain.

## Confirmation (AC-004-01)

After a 201 response the form is removed and an element with role `status` shows the heading `Registration received`, the participant's first and last name, and a list of the display names of the selected options.
